clue.text: There's opening to nick lags with dragnet cast around here

definitions.text: There's opening to nick lags with dragnet cast around here

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of the following word is kept
to cast is to throw or mould, so the gathered letters are thrown into a new shape

blocks.note: first letter of nick
taken as written; lags are old convicts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police sweep through a criminal district, nabbing old lags with a net.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a district where you might nick lags with a dragnet is the criminal world.
explanation.definitionFit: The criminal underworld is where convicts and crooks congregate, the natural place to throw a police net.

clue.text: What was rank and ranker when picked up? Aussie bug

indicators.note: picked up means caught by the ear, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: an obsolete word for rank or degree; 'What was' flags the old usage
n is a short form of and, as in rock 'n' roll
ranker means more gross, said aloud

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that once was rank and grew ranker, answered by an Australian insect.
explanation.walkthrough: Rank looks like a noun for a soldier, but it is an old word meaning degree; ranker is the comparative of rank meaning gross.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia the common green cicada is popularly called by this shopkeeper's name.

clue.text: Web designers earn a smashing wage on a regular basis

indicators.note: something smashed is broken up and its pieces fall into a new order
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
second and fourth letters of wage

explanation.surface: Website designers who earn a terrific wage week in, week out.
explanation.walkthrough: Web designers sounds like internet professionals, but it means the spiders that spin webs.
explanation.definitionFit: The zoological order of spiders, creatures that construct webs, bears this Latin name.

clue.text: Bard's merry old poem recalled after new one

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
I is the Roman numeral one
dit is an archaic word for a ditty or poem

explanation.surface: A cheerful old poem by Shakespeare, remembered after a newer one.
explanation.walkthrough: Bard's marks the definition as a poetic, literary word rather than everyday English.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare poetic adjective means shining or bright, and in the gay, sparkling sense it covers merry.

clue.text: Problem boarding public transport around outskirts of town

indicators.note: a passenger boarding gets inside the vehicle, so one word goes inside the other
turned around means facing the other way, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a bus is public transport
a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: Trouble getting on a bus that loops round the edge of town.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential district lying on the edge of a town or city is exactly its outskirts.

clue.text: Sell slips in fashion shops

indicators.note: the first letter slips down to the back of the word
in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: ton means the fashion or the fashionable set
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sales drop in clothes shops.
explanation.walkthrough: Shops looks like a plural noun for stores, but it is a verb: to shop someone is British slang for informing on them.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray someone to the authorities is to inform against them, which is the slang verb sense.

clue.text: Drifters wear oversized trousers

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the following words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: Vagrants wearing baggy, oversized trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Trousers reads as the clothing, but it is a verb meaning pockets or holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderers with no fixed course are people who roam, just as drifters do.

clue.text: Rent reduction withdrawn, last in house leaves

indicators.note: something withdrawn is pulled back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
last picks only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: to let is to rent out
a cut is a reduction
final letter of house

explanation.surface: A rent cut is taken back, and the last tenant leaves the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves looks like a verb for departing tenants; it is the noun, the salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: This salad plant is grown and eaten for its green leaves.

clue.text: Animal — three letters — beginning with A

blocks.note: three letters starting at A run from A to C

explanation.surface: A word puzzle asking for a three-letter animal starting with A.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a three-letter animal, but the three letters are the stretch of alphabet itself, read as A, TO, C.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare Chambers word names a skunk, which is a mammal.

clue.text: Stars back on TV in a one off

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept
off means wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: last letter of TV
taken as written

explanation.surface: Celebrities return to television in a one-off special.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars suggests celebrities, which the TV comeback reinforces, but the definition is astronomical.
explanation.definitionFit: These are stars that suddenly flare to great brightness and then fade; the Latin plural is used.

clue.text: Wood stove's inside

indicators.note: only the interior of the word is kept, its two end letters dropped

blocks.note: a Primus is a portable camping stove; its middle letters are kept

explanation.surface: Wood burning in a stove.
explanation.walkthrough: Primus is a brand name for a paraffin camping stove.
explanation.definitionFit: This New Zealand conifer yields a valued red timber.

clue.text: Environmentalists with prominence creating a stink

blocks.note: Friends of the Earth, the environmental campaign group
a tor is a rocky hill or prominence

explanation.surface: Green campaigners with a high profile kicking up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Creating a stink suggests making a fuss; here the stink is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a formal word for an offensive smell, especially a bodily one.

clue.text: Inhibitions about gift almost bewildered son

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
someone bewildered is all mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
pressie is informal British for a present
taken as written

explanation.surface: A son confused about a present develops hang-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychologically, holding desires or feelings down is a form of restraint, matching inhibitions.

clue.text: Any food that can be cured. (Turkey excluded)

definitions.note: an eatable is a noun here, any item of food

indicators.note: excluded means left out, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: a condition that can be cured is curable by treatment
TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

explanation.surface: A note that any curable food is fine, except turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: Cured food suggests bacon or ham, and turkey the bird; here cured means healed and Turkey is the country code.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun this word means anything fit to be eaten, so any foodstuff.

clue.text: Part of bride's outfit? It'll arrive after June 30, and the rest apparently

blocks.note: July 1, written JUL I with the Roman numeral one, follows June 30
etc. stands for et cetera, and the rest
ap is an abbreviation for apparent or apparently

explanation.surface: A wedding outfit item ordered for a summer bride, arriving after the end of June.
explanation.definitionFit: A small close-fitting skullcap of the kind worn by Shakespeare's heroine is often worn by brides with a veil.

clue.text: Celtic hooligans due to leave Dundee's ground

indicators.note: the letters that leave are taken out of the word
ground means crushed up, so the remaining letters are broken and reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; each of its letters is removed once

explanation.surface: Celtic football fans due to be thrown out of Dundee's stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Celtic looks like the Glasgow football club; it simply means Scottish here. Ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a young tearaway or lout is a ned, so the plural means Scottish yobs.

clue.text: More smart meters ultimately produce recipe to cut excess usage

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept
to cut is to remove, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: last letter of meters
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take
OD, overdose, is excessive use of a drug

explanation.surface: Smart meters are meant to give a recipe for cutting excessive energy use.
explanation.walkthrough: Smart meters reads as the home energy device; smart belongs with More and means neatly turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and trim in appearance, and this comparative form means neater or smarter.

clue.text: Summerhouse view that's amazing overlooking Yarmouth's front

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
overlooking means ignoring, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: to gaze is to view
boy! is an exclamation of amazement
first letter of Yarmouth

explanation.surface: A summerhouse with an amazing view, overlooking the seafront at Yarmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Overlooking sounds like having a view over the front, but it means disregarding a letter. Great Yarmouth is an English seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: A small open garden building giving a view, often used in summer, is a classic pavilion.

clue.text: Ant does this when first appearing, Dec starting late fails

definitions.text: Ant does this when first appearing

indicators.note: a late start means the opening letter is missing

blocks.note: taken as written
to lose is to fail

explanation.surface: Ant and Dec, the British TV presenting duo, with Dec arriving late and flopping.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a famous British TV double act; here the ant is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect emerging from its pupa or egg is said to do this, the moment it first appears as an adult.

clue.text: Launch of newspaper, a vital year to come out

indicators.note: the letter that comes out is removed from the word

blocks.note: taken as written
FT, the Financial Times newspaper
taken as written
key means vital or crucial
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Launching a newspaper, with a crucial year still to come.
explanation.walkthrough: Launch of newspaper reads as one phrase, but only Launch is the definition and of is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare noun means the act of taking off, as an aircraft or rocket does at a launch.

clue.text: Let off a bit of steam, but you've no right to swear

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece, here its first letter
no means without, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: first letter of steam
to curse is to swear
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Venting your frustration is fine, but you have no right to use bad language.
explanation.walkthrough: Let off a bit of steam reads as one idiom, but Let off is the definition: to pardon.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a colloquial clipped form of excuse, meaning to pardon or let someone go unpunished.

clue.text: Meeting overran, I messed up somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the words is used
in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: found spanning these words

explanation.surface: Someone admits a meeting ran late because they slipped up a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of students or professionals for discussion is a type of meeting.

clue.text: Not hard to get to the answer

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: to reach is to get to
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
t' is a dialect form of the

explanation.surface: Finding the answer isn't difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer looks like a noun, the solution, but it is the verb, to respond.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond to something is to answer it with a response or reply.

clue.text: Back in the shivering parts of December and January

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
shivering means trembling, shaking these letters into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
to back a horse is to bet on it

explanation.surface: Feeling the cold during the shivering winter weeks of December and January.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is singular in sense though worded as parts: one month spanning parts of both.
explanation.definitionFit: This month of the Jewish calendar falls across late December and early January.

clue.text: Finishes off latte and exits after breaking cafe stools

indicators.note: breaking smashes the word apart so its letters can be reassembled
finishes are ends, so the last letters of the next words are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of latte
last letter of exits

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a latte and storms out after smashing up the cafe's stools.
explanation.walkthrough: Stools sits naturally as cafe furniture; the definition is the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine stools are bowel motions, which is the waste matter this word names.

clue.text: Collage is toneless to some extent, I'm not keen on the greys

definitions.text: I'm not keen on the greys

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the words is used

blocks.note: found spanning these words

explanation.surface: An art critic dismissing a dull grey collage.
explanation.walkthrough: Greys reads as dull colours from the collage, but it means grey-haired, older people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prejudiced against the elderly would say they dislike grey-haired people.

clue.text: Yahoo stocks leak circulating — may fall in autumn

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so these letters are moved about
to stock is to hold within, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a yahoo is a boor, an oaf
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Yahoo and stocks paint a tech-shares story; yahoo is the old word for a lout, and stocks means holds.
explanation.definitionFit: The foliage of an oak tree drops in autumn, as deciduous leaves do.

clue.text: Scandinavians idolised these famed skiers regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.walkthrough: Idolised suggests sporting fandom, but it is literal: these were worshipped as gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology these are the principal gods, led by Odin, worshipped by early Scandinavians.

clue.text: Forces to drop good practices

blocks.note: gism, a variant of jism, means energy or force
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.definitionFit: These are distinctive doctrines, practices or systems, such as those named with the suffix.

clue.text: Health resort with one sharing a room

explanation.walkthrough: Sharing a is an instruction: the two pieces overlap on their common letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: Room in the sense of available area or capacity is exactly this word.

clue.text: Monks pronounced Daniel's boast on leaving lion's den?

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the phrase is taken by its sound

blocks.clueFragment: Daniel's boast on leaving lion's den?
blocks.note: what Daniel could proudly say when he left the lions unharmed

explanation.surface: Monks retelling the Bible story of Daniel walking out of the lions' den.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Daniel he is thrown to the lions and emerges unhurt, hence his boast.

clue.text: US moles name corrupt leader of Liberia exiled

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name

first letter of Liberia

clue.text: A Spain trip? Essentially too homey maybe for Spaniard

middle letter of too

explanation.walkthrough: Homey looks like the adjective for homely; it is US slang for a pal from your home town.
explanation.definitionFit: This Spanish word means a fellow countryman or friend, the equivalent of the slang homie.

clue.text: Stir crazy, very close to insane inside clinks

indicators.note: crazy means wild or deranged, so these letters are scrambled
the close of a word is its end, so its last letter is kept
inside puts these pieces within the other

blocks.note: taken as written

last letter of insane

explanation.surface: A prisoner going stir crazy, very nearly insane, inside the jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir and clink are both slang for prison, so the surface is a jail story; clinks is a verb meaning clinches.
explanation.definitionFit: To clink is a Scots verb meaning to fasten or clinch, which is what a metal fastener of this kind does.

clue.text: Play this possibly for a calypso

definitions.text: Play this possibly for a calypso

clue.text: Back from dentist, sister is struggling with her canines

taken as written
taken as written
